format: Authored SVG architecture diagrams; PNG social previews

diagrams.alt: The login server sends a secret keytab to the application server over HTTPS without client authentication. A dashed route shows that another reachable client knowing the URL could obtain it too.
diagrams.caption: The application download succeeded. The dashed route shows possible access by another reachable client; no theft was observed.
diagrams.title: AI Made Authentication Keys Downloadable Without Login

diagrams.alt: A PostgreSQL primary retains a private SSH key, while two standbys still authorize that key for root login after setup.
diagrams.caption: The root SSH access was used for setup and retained afterward. A later compromise of the primary could expose this route to reachable standbys that still accept the key.
diagrams.title: AI Left Root SSH Access After a Transfer

diagrams.alt: Requested access allows one named client to reach an upload service. The configured rule admits the whole firewall zone, including other clients whose access was not tested.
diagrams.caption: Requested access versus the configured firewall rule. Only the named client’s connection was tested.
diagrams.title: AI Opened More Firewall Access Than Requested

diagrams.alt: Two DHCP servers share one network segment. Clients continue receiving addresses from the existing responder; the newly started dnsmasq server records no leases.
diagrams.caption: Both DHCP servers were on the same segment. Clients continued using the existing responder, while the new server recorded no leases.
diagrams.title: AI Started a Competing DHCP Server
